Snakebite Emergency Care: Restrict movement and keep bite locations immobilized below heart level during evacuation.

Step 4 - Transport Evacuation: Document incident coordinates and move injured personnel to the nearest roadway access.

misconception_pool.misconception: Beginners often believe standard office adhesive bandages provide adequate field treatment for survey injuries.
misconception_pool.fact: Survey parties require rugged trauma kits containing pressure bandages, splints, and insect bite treatments.

misconception_pool.misconception: Burning an attached tick with a match or coating it in petroleum jelly forces it to back out safely.
misconception_pool.fact: Heat or suffocation causes the tick to regurgitate infectious fluids into the wound; grasp it near the skin with fine tweezers and pull up.

misconception_pool.misconception: Cutting a snakebite wound and sucking out the venom reduces the amount of toxin entering the bloodstream.
misconception_pool.fact: Incising or sucking a snakebite damages blood vessels and introduces bacteria; keep the victim calm, immobilize the limb, and get medical help.

misconception_pool.misconception: Pinching a bee stinger between your thumb and forefinger is the fastest way to stop venom injection.
misconception_pool.fact: Squeezing the venom sac injects more toxin into the skin; scrape the stinger sideways using the edge of a credit card or dull knife blade.

misconception_pool.misconception: Drinking a large bottle of ice water all at once is the safest treatment for a surveyor with heat exhaustion.
misconception_pool.fact: Gulping cold water can trigger severe stomach cramps and vomiting; move the person to shade, cool the skin, and give small sips of water.

Step 4 - Closure Verification: Resight the initial backsight corner to verify that orientation drifted zero seconds.

misconception_pool.fact: Radial surveying requires resighting the initial reference mark to prove the instrument maintained horizontal orientation.

misconception_pool.misconception: Leveling the transit head with the leveling screws automatically keeps the optical plummet centered over the corner tack.
misconception_pool.fact: Adjusting leveling screws tilts the vertical axis slightly; always recheck and recenter the optical plummet or plumb bob after final leveling.

misconception_pool.misconception: Pulling a survey tape along the ground slope gives the true horizontal distance required for boundary calculations.
misconception_pool.fact: Boundary plats require horizontal distances; surveyors must either hold the tape level with a plumb bob or apply a slope angle correction.

misconception_pool.misconception: Erasing a mistaken distance in the field notebook keeps legal survey records cleaner and more accurate.
misconception_pool.fact: Erasing destroys original legal evidence in a field book; cross out errors with a single line and write the corrected value neatly above it.

misconception_pool.misconception: Sighting the top of a tilted range pole yields the same horizontal angle as sighting the bottom tip on the corner tack.
misconception_pool.fact: A range pole held out of plumb shifts the line of sight horizontally; always sight the lowest visible point near the tack or plumb the pole.

misconception_pool.misconception: Novices often believe architectural scales marked in fractional inches are identical to decimal civil engineering scales.

misconception_pool.misconception: Measuring decimal feet on a plat with a standard 16ths-of-an-inch ruler produces exact engineering scale lengths.

misconception_pool.misconception: Radial angles recorded from a reference corner are plotted by moving the protractor center to each newly drawn perimeter point.
misconception_pool.fact: All radial angles were turned from a single instrument station, so the protractor must stay centered on that station aligned to the baseline.

misconception_pool.misconception: Magnetic north and true geodetic north point in the exact same direction on a property survey map.
misconception_pool.fact: Magnetic north differs from true north by the local magnetic declination angle, so a survey plat must note which north reference is shown.

misconception_pool.misconception: Written distances and acreage numbers in a deed always override physical boundary monuments found in the ground.

misconception_pool.misconception: A utility easement recorded in a property deed transfers ownership of that strip of land to the utility company.

misconception_pool.misconception: A quitclaim deed guarantees that the grantor holds clear, unencumbered title and surveyed boundaries to the parcel.
misconception_pool.fact: A quitclaim deed transfers only whatever interest the grantor currently possesses, whereas a warranty deed guarantees clear title and defense.

misconception_pool.misconception: Standard drone camera photogrammetry can measure bare-earth ground elevations directly through a closed, leafy forest canopy.
misconception_pool.fact: Optical photogrammetry only maps visible top surfaces like leaves, whereas LiDAR laser pulses penetrate small canopy gaps to hit bare ground.

misconception_pool.misconception: Consumer drone GPS receivers alone achieve survey-grade centimeter accuracy without ground control points or RTK corrections.
misconception_pool.fact: Standard autonomous drone GPS drifts by several feet; survey-grade accuracy requires Ground Control Points or RTK/PPK carrier-phase corrections.

misconception_pool.misconception: A single terrestrial laser scanner setup can capture every wall and surface of a building without any blind spots.
misconception_pool.fact: Laser scanners are strictly line-of-sight instruments, so surveyors must register scans from multiple stations to eliminate shadow occlusions.

misconception_pool.misconception: Beginners often assume survey satellite receivers operate identically to smartphone navigation chips.
misconception_pool.fact: Survey GNSS receivers track dual-frequency carrier waves and utilize base station differential corrections for centimeter accuracy.

misconception_pool.misconception: Surveyors using GPS equipment transmit radio signals up to the satellites in orbit to request their ground coordinates.
misconception_pool.fact: GPS satellites are one-way broadcast beacons; ground receivers only listen to timed signals and compute position by trilateration.

misconception_pool.misconception: Three GPS satellites are sufficient to determine exact latitude, longitude, and elevation on a standard survey receiver.
misconception_pool.fact: A fourth satellite signal is mandatory to solve for the timing clock bias between the receiver's quartz clock and the satellite atomic clocks.

misconception_pool.misconception: Handheld hiking GPS units and survey-grade RTK GNSS rovers use the same signal measurement method and achieve identical accuracy.
misconception_pool.fact: Consumer GPS reads coarse code signals accurate to several meters, while survey RTK receivers track carrier-wave phase for centimeter accuracy.

misconception_pool.misconception: Closely clustered satellites directly overhead provide better geometric dilution of precision than satellites spread across the sky.
misconception_pool.fact: Satellites bunched together create poor geometry and high PDOP error; wide angular separation across the sky yields the strongest 3D position.
